commands.command: deno eval lifecycle and evidence counterexamples

evidence: PILOT-001-R1-001 and PILOT-001-R1-005 demonstrate acceptance without mandatory lifecycle, review, and evidence closure.
PILOT-001-R1-003 leaves an availability/resource-exhaustion path through repeated references.
PILOT-001-R1-001, PILOT-001-R1-002, and PILOT-001-R1-004 violate exact state, review, and content-address contracts.
PILOT-001-R1-003 shows unbounded repeated referenced-file I/O and allocation.
The implementation is dependency-free, organized into focused helpers, formatted, lint-clean, and type-clean.
The authentic RED and 100 percent coverage gates pass, but semantic mutants in PILOT-001-R1-001, R1-002, R1-004, and R1-005 survive.

findings.expectedBehavior: Acceptance requires a lifecycle ending at the declared phase and an APPROVED exact-candidate fresh review with six satisfactory lenses and no unresolved finding.
findings.observedBehavior: A review-phase packet with empty reviewRefs and reviews validates after only candidate/check fields are populated; empty evidence collections and a ledger that ends at review are accepted.
findings.reproduction: Starting from the valid fixture, empty results, reviews, refs, events, and checks; null both candidate fields; keep phase accepted and requiredTasks empty. Validation returns no issues.
findings.impact: A controller can manufacture acceptance without TDD evidence, lifecycle closure, or independent review.
findings.requiredRemediation: Add phase-aware minimum cardinalities and enforce exact ticket, revision, round, actor, result, review, candidate, and final-event relationships.
findings.verification: Add table-driven mutants for empty records, mismatched IDs/revisions/rounds/runs, nonterminal ledgers, absent approved review, failed lenses, and CHANGES_REQUESTED verdicts.

findings.expectedBehavior: Strict packets reject malformed primitive types, empty evidence, invalid enums, unknown references, and contradictory review semantics; templates must instantiate valid records.
findings.observedBehavior: Non-string revisions, paths, and hashes bypass checks; review verdict and finding values are weakly constrained; the result template supplies a null dispatchRef.
findings.reproduction: Set ticket.baseRevision or a test digest to 42, review verdict to an arbitrary value, or required finding values to null; the relevant stable diagnostic is absent.
findings.impact: Meaningless or forged evidence can satisfy the mechanical acceptance shape.
findings.requiredRemediation: Validate all primitive types, non-empty strings, enums, unique IDs/paths/tasks, finding criterion/contract/lens references, verdict-lens-finding consistency, and make dispatchRef a required safe path.
findings.verification: Add table-driven negative tests for every malformed primitive, enum, empty string, duplicate, unknown reference, and contradictory review combination.

findings.expectedBehavior: CLI input count, aggregate bytes, and repeated work are deterministically bounded.
findings.observedBehavior: A sub-1 MB state file can contain thousands of duplicate result/review references, causing the same near-1 MB file to be read, parsed, and retained repeatedly.
findings.reproduction: Create thousands of repeated results/r.json references and one near-limit JSON file; the CLI performs one read and parse per duplicate.
findings.impact: Corrupt ticket data can exhaust CI or reviewer memory and CPU despite per-file limits.
findings.requiredRemediation: Bound and deduplicate references and collections, cap aggregate bytes/records before parsing, and emit stable limit diagnostics.
findings.verification: Add CLI tests for duplicate refs, over-limit counts, and aggregate-byte exhaustion that fail before unbounded reads.

findings.expectedBehavior: RED and candidate revisions exist, ancestry is valid, declared RED test hashes match Git blobs, and the RED diff contains no production change.
findings.observedBehavior: The validator checks only 40/64-character patterns; nonexistent all-zero revisions and fabricated hashes validate.
findings.reproduction: Replace redRevision, candidateRevision, and each SHA-256 with syntactically valid nonexistent values in an otherwise valid fixture; structural validation emits no content-address issue.
findings.impact: Fabricated RED/candidate evidence can manufacture compliance with the mandatory TDD gate.
findings.requiredRemediation: At the CLI boundary, resolve commit objects and ancestry, hash declared files from redRevision, compare the RED diff with declared test/check and ticket-evidence paths, and audit candidate changed paths against allowedWrites.
findings.verification: Use a temporary Git repository to test nonexistent revisions, wrong hashes, production changes in RED, stale/non-descendant candidates, and a genuine valid lineage.

findings.expectedBehavior: Every declared result, review, dispatch, phase log, event evidence, and accepted-state artifact exists as a bounded regular file under the ticket directory and maps exactly to its record.
findings.observedBehavior: The valid-directory test omits dispatch and phase log files yet passes; invalid-prefix refs are silently skipped, and no acceptance artifact is required.
findings.reproduction: Run the current valid-directory fixture without creating dispatch or log files, or point resultRefs at evidence/ignored.json; the CLI does not emit the required missing/unsafe-reference diagnostic.
findings.impact: The CLI can approve fabricated or absent execution/review evidence.
findings.requiredRemediation: Reject every invalid, duplicate, or unmapped reference and verify safe containment, existence, file type, size, and round correspondence for all evidence; require acceptance.md only in accepted/integrated phases.
findings.verification: Add directory-level negative tests for missing, wrong-prefix, duplicate, non-file, oversized, mismatched-round, and escaped evidence plus a complete valid directory.

notes: PILOT-001-R1-004 and PILOT-001-R1-005 were added by the orchestrator from a second independent clean-context adversarial audit.
The PostgreSQL 18.4/17.10 matrix passed from the integration checkout; the linked worktree exposes a pre-existing line-ending-sensitive audit-hash limitation without changing schema files.
